config.title: Build drag and drop list reordering

intro.title: Build drag and drop list reordering
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive list where you can drag and drop items to reorder them. You will learn how to handle mouse events like mousedown, mousemove, and mouseup to track dragging behavior. The core programming concept involves managing state to track the dragged item's position and updating the list order accordingly. You'll use basic JavaScript, HTML, and CSS to create a visual, functional drag-and-drop interface.
intro.usecase: Drag-and-drop list reordering is essential for creating intuitive user interfaces where manual organization is required. Developers implement this pattern in dashboard widgets, allowing users to customize their workspace by rearranging charts and data panels. Content management systems use it for sorting media galleries or adjusting menu item hierarchies, while project management tools rely on it for prioritizing task lists and kanban cards. This functionality transforms static displays into interactive experiences where users control their visual layout and workflow.

objectives: Initialize state variables to track drag-and-drop interactions
Implement drag event handlers for list items
Apply drop logic to reorder list items in the DOM
Configure visual feedback during drag operations
Integrate drag-and-drop functionality into a list component
Manipulate array data to reflect reordered items
Construct a complete drag-and-drop reordering interface

// Create the App component here

steps.title: Initialize state for the list items
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, use the useState hook to create a state variable named 'items' initialized with an array of strings like ['Item 1', 'Item 2', 'Item 3', 'Item 4'].
steps.hint: Call useState with an array of strings as the initial value, and destructure the returned array into a variable named 'items' and a setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: initializing state with an array
const [todos, setTodos] = useState(['Task 1', 'Task 2', 'Task 3']);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'items' containing an array of strings, ready to be displayed and reordered later.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an array of strings, and the destructured variable is named 'items'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an array of strings and naming the variable 'items'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Use useState to create a state variable 'items' initialized with an array of strings like ['Item 1', 'Item 2', 'Item 3', 'Item 4'].

steps.title: Add state for tracking dragged item
steps.instruction: Inside your App component, add another useState hook to track the currently dragged item. Declare a state variable named 'draggedItem' and initialize it to null.
steps.hint: You'll need to call useState again with an initial value of null, and destructure the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: tracking a selected item
const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a second state variable to track which item is being dragged during drag-and-drop operations.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that declares 'draggedItem' state variable initialized to null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared the state variable exactly as 'draggedItem' and initialized it to null.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a second useState hook inside your component to track the dragged item with a variable named 'draggedItem' set to null initially.

steps.instruction: Inside your App component, define a function named handleDragStart that takes an index parameter and sets the draggedItem state to that index.
steps.hint: Create a function that updates the draggedItem state when a drag operation starts.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleDragStart function will be called when a drag starts on a list item, storing its index in state.
successCriteria: Function sets draggedItem state to the index
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function takes an index parameter and updates the draggedItem state with that index.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function called handleDragStart that sets the draggedItem state to the index passed as a parameter.

steps.title: Define handleDrop function
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleDrop that takes a dropIndex parameter. Inside it, create a new array copy of items, remove the dragged item from its original position, insert it at dropIndex,
steps.hint: You can use the spread operator to copy the items array, then use splice to remove and insert the dragged item at the correct positions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The handleDrop function is defined with dropIndex parameter and implements the reordering logic.
successCriteria: handleDrop function is defined, creates a new array copy, removes dragged item, inserts it at dropIndex, updates items state, and resets draggedItem.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function handles all the steps: copy array, remove dragged item, insert at dropIndex, update state, and reset draggedItem.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleDrop function isn't defined correctly. Check that it takes dropIndex, creates a new array, removes the dragged item, inserts it, updates state, and resets draggedItem.

steps.title: Map and render list items
steps.instruction: Inside the list container, map over the items state to render each item as a div with className 'list-item', displaying the item text.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the items array to create an array of JSX elements. Each element should be a div with the class 'list-item' and the item text as content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The list container now contains four div elements with class 'list-item', each displaying one of the item texts from the state array.
successCriteria: The items state is mapped to render div elements with className 'list-item', each displaying the corresponding item text.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The list items aren't being rendered correctly. Remember to use the map method on the items state array to create JSX elements for each item.

steps.title: Wire drag and drop events to list items
steps.instruction: Add the drag and drop event handlers to each list item div inside the map function. Include draggable='true', onDragStart={() => handleDragStart(index)}, onDragOver={handleDragOver}, and onDrop={() => handleDrop(index)}.
steps.hint: Add the event handlers as attributes to the div that renders each item. Make sure to pass the current index to onDragStart and onDrop.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each list item will now be draggable and respond to drag and drop events, enabling reordering.
successCriteria: Each list item div has draggable='true', onDragStart, onDragOver, and onDrop handlers correctly attached.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some event handlers, but check that all required attributes (draggable, onDragStart, onDragOver, onDrop) are present on each list item div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The list items are missing the drag and drop event handlers. Make sure to add draggable='true' and the three event handlers to each div inside the map.
